decisions.reason: As a niche particle-therapy product it likely faces a smaller market and some rollout risk, but it remains closely tied to the firm's dosimetry capabilities so management would more likely keep it unless results clearly fall below aspiration levels.

This small-volume ionization chamber fits the firm's core measurement business, and absent clear evidence of underperformance a boundedly rational management would continue it while learning from accumulated market use.

Because it overlaps with other chamber offerings it is somewhat more exposed to comparative underperformance and portfolio rationalisation, but it is still close enough to the core business to be retained for now.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line sits at the heart of the firm's established offering, so it is unlikely to be withdrawn unless it delivers an unusually clear shortfall versus aspirations.

The relative-dosimetry chamber serves a specialist but relevant clinical use case, and management would usually keep such a product unless limited demand and resource pressures make its performance fall short of expectations.
